data.title: Production Metadata Embedded in Distributed Content Assets
data.summary:
Images, PDFs or videos distributed as campaign content carry embedded production
metadata — editing application, system locale, device model, GPS coordinates, a
"last saved by" field — inconsistent with the asset's claimed origin.
data.description:
This is the cheapest check available against a campaign asset and the one most often
skipped, because it rarely survives past the first post. Most platforms strip EXIF and
re-encode video on upload, so the tell is usually only present on the earliest-generation
copy — the original post, a linked download, or a mirror a less careful platform never
touched — and absent from every viral re-share after it.

What is worth pulling: a camera model or GPS tag inconsistent with the claimed location;
a PDF's producer application and XMP language setting inconsistent with the claimed
author's tooling; an Office document's author, company or "last modified by" field,
often left in a script the claimed author does not use; a video container's encoder
string and creation timestamp, which carries a timezone offset of its own.

The absence of any of this proves nothing on its own: an attentive operator scrubs
metadata deliberately, and a platform's own re-encoding does the same thing by accident.
Treat a clean asset as inconclusive, not as evidence the asset is genuine. This finding
is about the campaign's own distributed content; it is a different check from
reconnaissance against a target organisation's own documents, which the OSINT discipline
covers separately.
data.recommendation:
* Pull metadata from the earliest-generation copy of the asset, not a re-share — most
  platforms strip EXIF and re-encode video on upload, which erases the tell from
  everything posted after the first instance.
* Preserve the original file before raising it with the platform or the public; a
  takedown report is also a deletion of the evidence.
* Treat a metadata-clean asset as inconclusive rather than exculpatory; scrubbing and
  platform re-encoding produce the same absence a genuinely clean asset would.
* Where metadata is present, cross-reference device model, GPS and locale fields against
  the claimed origin, and weigh the result alongside the corpus's other tells rather than
  citing it alone.
data.short_recommendation: Pull metadata from the earliest-generation copy before it is stripped, and treat a clean result as inconclusive.
